title: The Second to Last Week :(
The beginning
content:
My four month long journey started in O'Hare where I hugged my parents goodbye and made my way through security.


My flight left at 3:50 P.M. Central Time and was about 7 hours to Dublin International Airport.  I was super excited that we flew over Elk Grove and I got to see my house! Even if that meant I was that annoying airplane that interrupted someones conversation down on the ground in Elk Grove.


The plane ride went flawlessly and I arrived here at 5:00 A.M local time. The city looked beautiful at night.



The airport was pretty dead when I arrived and I decided to catch up on some sleep in this cool looking cubby hole.

After a couple hours, I woke up to a bustling atmosphere.  I'm getting pretty excited for this trip after spent my first Euros on coffee ( thanks Aunt Kathy!! ), and hearing many different languages around the airport. Already, I can see cultural differences. I saw a store in the airport dedicated to rugby,  different snack food and candies, and in the way people dress.

 I'm excited, but slightly nervous for this incredible immersion opportunity. I will be posting later this week after I arrive and settle in in Bilbao!

title: New Foods and a Weekend to Madrid and Toledo
content:
This post is long. I'm not gunna lie to you, but if you just wanna read parts of it, there is a section on foods I've been eating here, the Athletic Bilbao vs Real Madrid game, and also on my weekend trip to Madrid and Toledo.  Nevertheless, we will start from the beginning

So on Sunday, we were put into contact with a girl named Bri.  She studied here in Bilbao last semester and graduated last May.  Her previous host family did not have a student this semester and asked Bri if she wanted to return and stay with them for free.  Of course she accepted and so now she is here!

It’s been really nice to talk to her.  She has a lot off advice and recommendations for things to do and places to go.

On Tuesday night I we met up in a café in Bilbao to play our trip to London!  It was kind of stressful because the hotels are last minute and a kind of expensive.  However, we got everything done. We won’t be sleeping on benches.  We haven’t made our plans for activities yet in London, but a couple of us planned a day trip to the Dover.  I’m so excited for this! The White Cliffs are so beautiful!



The hot chocolate here is way different than anything you have ever had.  It’s very think, like very thick. It’s as if they melted a big piece of chocolate into a tiny bit of milk. It’s pretty incredible.  We also had churros with our chocolate.



Bri brought along a couple Spanish friends to the café and it was nice to talk to them in Spanish.  I’m getting more comfortable talking with locals in Spanish and being comfortable with making mistakes.

Since not much happened in the beginning of the week, I am going to do a little catch up on the food that I’ve been eating!!

FOOD


So Begoña is a fantastic cook! She cooks basically all of my meals.  The food has been absolutely delicious, and I have been a little adventurous and tried some new foods.  Some of the foods here are Basque and so you won't find them in other parts of Spain.

So this meal right here is pretty typical.  You have some amazing sausage on the left.  Flan (its like a slightly harder pudding) is up on the top left.  Tomato salad with plenty of oil and vinegar is on the top right.  Front and center is a "tortilla". Its not a normal tortilla by any means.  Its more like an omelet. It really is an omelet, but it has lots of sliced potatoes in it.  Its awesome!!


Here is something that I might have for dinner.  Dinners tend to be small, more like a snack because they have such big lunches.  So this is Iberian ham and some kind of cheese.  The ham is soooooo good! I love it! At first when she put it on my plate I thought it was just uncooked bacon and I was freaking out!


I had this for dessert this week. Its called a butter cookie.  Its basically a graham cracker that she put butter in between.  It was kinda gross.


Okay, so remember when I told you that I was being adventurous? Here it is.
So you can see that at the bottom is an oil soaked salad.  Its not that bad, you just have to let it drip dry a little.  On the top left is some pretty good fish.  I'm not sure what is was called, she just called it the white fish.  In the top middle, there is some octopus.  Yup, I had octopus.  I was surprised that I went through with eating it, but it actually wasn't that bad, just really salty and chewy. 


Second big step: Anchovies. One day my host mom asked me if I liked anchovies and I didn't know what to say, so I just said that I never had tried them.  This was true, but she took it as an invitation to enlighten me.  

This is what I was served. Anchovies right out of a tin, served up on some bread.  It was okay, if you haven't had them before, I promise you won't die.  They are just like a really salty fish.


I guess she didn't think I had enough, so I had fried anchovies later that week.  These ones were better, they didn't taste as strong because they were fried.  It did sketch me out that I had to pull the tails off though


Athletic vs Real Madrid


So as soon as we arrived to Bilbao at the beginning of September, a couple of us had been talking about going to the Real Madrid game.  We didn’t think that we were going to get tickets and we thought that they were going to be very expensive.  However, my friend Alex bought tickets for us for 50 Euro! I thought the tickets were going to be much more expensive and then I wouldn't be able to go!



The game was great!! It atmosphere was much different than the Augsburg game.  There was a lot of hatred for Ronaldo.  Whenever he was close to the ball, the entire stadium was booing him.  Everyone was very into the game and very emotional about everything.  If a player went down, or there was some kind of penalty, everyone jumped out of their seats and started yelling and swearing at the ref.


 It was so much fun.  Even though we lost 1-2, I still went home feeling amazing even though I lost my voice.  It was worth every penny.

Side note: This whole sandwich thing at half time is so weird to me.  When I say that “everyone pulls out a sandwich”, I’m not exaggerating. I think like 97% of the crowd brings one. The other 3% are foreigners. It’s ridiculous. You can see in the picture there are like 15 sandwiches, and there are like 10 more that you can’t see. It’s so bizarre.



Madrid trip!


We had to be at the school at 8:00 am on Friday, which means that I would need to wake up at 6:30 to have time to shower and catch the metro.  But I woke up at 7:15 because I forgot to plug my phone in and it died.  Ooops. But everything was fine! I made it to the bus just in time and I had to skip the shower, but at least got a little run in on my way to catch the bus!  

I tried to write some of this post on the bus, but I kept getting distracted by the views outside the window.  


The drive was 5 hours to Madrid and it was a great opportunity to see the Spanish country side. Much of the land was used for farming, but I’m not sure what because nothing had grown yet.


 I did see quite a few olive tree groves and sunflower patches.


As we approached Madrid, we saw a couple of beautiful mountain peaks.


There aren’t very many skyscrapers in Madrid, but the ones we did see were kinda funky, but I like it!


We dropped our stuff off in the hotel and headed off to go sightseeing!


First stop was the Palacio Real.

This Palace is just jaw dropping.  I’ve never been in a palace before and I think this was a great one to start with.  We entered into the “court yard” in between the Cathedral of Almudena and the Palace.  Don’t fret. I took a sphere!!

Palacio Real

I loved this space.  The architecture was incredible and the view off to the west was incredible.  If only I could have gotten rid of all those other tourists.




We also took a jumping picture in front of the Palacio Real and I don’t think I have ever felt more touristy in my life.


We started on our tour and we could only take pictures in the first little landing. I am so sad that I am not able to share the inside off the beautiful building.


We walked through about 15 rooms and each room had a different theme.  It was incredible to see the amount of money dumped into each room. The wall paper in one of the rooms was all embroidery.  The rooms were littered with intricate marble carvings on molding, embellishment with precious stones, large paintings, hand carved wooden chairs, and statues.

I actually snuck in a picture of this sign because I thought it was hilarious that the dressing the King was referred to as a ceremony.


The dining room was especially interesting. There was an enormous table with room for over 140 people.  The ceiling was a giant mural. The walls were riddled with marble statues and large paintings.  In the center was the kings throne.  Two gold lions guarded the throne.  Above the throne was was the Spanish coat of arms.



 This has been a symbol of Spain for a long time and also was the reason for the $ symbol.  During the time when Europe was claiming new territories and exploring the world, Spain was very powerful.  Their money was minted with this symbol of two poles with ribbons. Its pretty easy to see how this translated into money symbol.  The two poles became the two vertical bars and the ribbons was represented as that “S”, that goes over them. 

When we left the palace, we had a short little tour of the rest of Madrid. We saw the Mercado de San Miguel.



We also saw the Plaza Mayor.


  I love the painted facades.


We then ventured over to the Puerto del Sol. I was really overwhelmed with how many people there were.  Sooooo many tourists and vendors everywhere!



I stepped on the supposed center of Spain.  This point is supposed to be the origin of all the roads in Spain.


We returned back to the hotel for a buffet lunch.  I had pretty low expectations, but I was blow out of the water. The food was great and there was a lot of it! I definitely ate too much.


After dinner, we went back up to our room and played cards.  I learned Euker!
  


The next morning we woke up bright and early to grab a quick breakfast and head out to Toledo. Toledo is an interesting city.  So many different people have influenced this city.  The Jews first settled in the city, then the Romans took over the town, then later the Moors conquered Toledo. The Christians, Muslims and Jews lived in coexistence until the Christians claimed the town.  However, the did not pillage the town.  In fact, the opened translation centers to translate Arab books into Castillian and Latin.




We met a up with a tour guide inside and immediately headed up a hill for a view of the city.  This view was one of my favorite parts of this trip.  Its absolutely amazing view of this old city. 


Aqueducts were used to bring water from the mountains into the city.


The tour guide explained to us that there is a law that all buildings must be constructed to fit in.  Only materials like rock, brick, ceramic, and clay can be used.  For example, this quaint house is actually a "discoteca" or a club. 


Next we hopped off and toured the 15th Century Toledo Cathedral.  This was so incredible.  From the outside it appears to be incredible, but the inside is just a world of its own. 


I didn't spend that much time listening to the tour guide, because I was so focused on looking around and taking it all in.  The ceilings were the most impressive to me, there are 88 columns and they are 120 meters tall. 


When I took this photosphere, I really didn't think it would turn out because it was so dark, but it looks good.  You can start to comprehend how large this building was.

Toledo Cathedral

The chorus is a huge deal at this cathedral, and you can really see why.  So much work went into this area.  Everything in this room was hand carved from either wood, marble or ivory.



To go along with the impressive chorus, you need an impressive organ!


We went in this tiny room and saw The Great Monstrance of Arfe.  It took 5 years to build it is over 10 feet tall.  The whole thing is made up of over 183 kilos of gold.  Thats over 300 lbs! 


The whole thing can be dismantled because it is made up of 6,00 unscrewable pieces.  This was done twice; once to hide it from Napoleon and another time to protect it during the Spanish Civil War.


After the Cathedral we had a few minutes of free time before lunch.  We checked out this beautiful art form called demascara.  The name comes from the town of Damascus and the craft was brought by the Jews.


Basically you hammer pieces of gold into steel and then cure it in a special way.  


We had lunch and then hopped on the bus back to Madrid. 



Potatoes with a weird food.  It was a flaky pastry like bread with beef in the middle and covered in a sweet sauce
Basically a Spanish take on lasagna

When we arrived back in Madrid we took off to see the Parque Retiro!!



Tourists being touristy
The book stores went on forever!

So when we finally got there, it was amazing! Its a giant park filled with trees and flowers and walking paths and ponds and gardens! Its a wonderful place!


There is even a tunnel!!!


Oh yah and we took this...


They had a big pond where you could rent row boats too!


When we were walking along this pond, I casually glanced over to me left, and I just about jumped out of my skin with excitement!! I saw out of the corner of my eye, a hand pan. Its the coolest instruments that I have ever heard.  I have only seen it on YouTube and this was the first time I had ever heard it in person! Here is a little recap of his performance!


Its so cool right!! Its so calming and smooth! It often gets paired with a didgeridoo and that sounds great!  I was so happy with this guy that I even bought his CD!
After I calmed down a little, we went over to the Temple of Debod. This temple was given to Spain by the Egyptians as a gift for helping them save the temples of Abu Simbel.


And here is a photosphere I took nearby!

Temple of Debod

SOOO! After that, we ran over to this thing called a Microteatro. Up top is a bar, but downstairs, there is 5 rooms that are about the size of a bathroom.  Each showing is 15 min and costs about $5.  15 people in each audience and there was two actors in our performance.  It was super tight in there if you can imagine... but it was really cool interesting idea and the show we saw was pretty funny!


After this we headed back to the hotel for dinner, This is where I made a mistake.  My friend Matt told me that they were serving cow intestines

 .  I though it sounded pretty gross but I figured I should try it.  I grabbed a scoop (what was I thinking!?!?) and sat down.  As soon as I sat down, I realized what I had done.  This stuffff stankkkk! I was sitting straight up away from my plate and it still smelled like I was standing in the middle of 10 stinky cows.  I stabbed a piece and dug in. 

I'm not gunna lie, I gagged a little, but in my defense, my friends were not helping by reminding me how bad it smells and telling me all the things that went through that cows stomach.  Nevertheless, I forced that piece down and now I can say that I tried cow intestines!

 The next morning, I woke up early enough to run up to the roof and still catch a little bit of the sunrise.


After a quick breakfast, we went over to the Museo Prado it is one of the biggest collections of European art in the world.  It was very big, but we only had 2 hours to spend there.  We had a short 1 hour tour, but I felt like the guide spoke Spanish that was a little to high level for me to fully grasp everything.  So I kind of wish that we had the full 2 hours to explore and read signs by ourselves.



we embarked on our 5 hr journey back home! All in all, I would say that Madrid isn't that special. Sure the Palace is cool and they have a nice art museum, but in the end, its just a big bustling city.  Its pretty generic.  Its filled with tourists and people.  There isn't that much culture or history.  Visiting Madrid made me much more sure with my decision to study in Bilbao.

Toledo on the other hand was excellent! I loved the architecture and the views and the size.  Granted it was still very tourist, but at least there was a better reason.  There was the cathedral and museums and history everywhere.

Since this post was so long, I'm going to leave out the things that I have learned, and save it for next week!

title: First weekend trip
content:
This was a packed week! One of my favorite things that we started doing was booking flights!! So far we have booked Poland and London! The next trip we are thinking about is to Mulan and Venice or maybe Greece.  I'm super excited to be able so see some other cities and experience the different cultures.

I have started a habit to duck into every bakery I see, and I don't think it will end well! Here is a delicious pastry that you see a lot around here.  I don't know what its called, but sometimes it takes other shapes, but either way it still has all of its flaky chocolaty goodness!


On Wednesday I had my visit to the embassy to deal with all my passport issues. If you would like to know all about that, check out my other blog post that goes in depth on that story.

Passport Story

On Thursday I went to my first soccer game here and it was just as awesome as everyone says. The team here is Athletic Bilbao, but you call the team Athletic (but its pronounced Aht-let-ee), never Athletic Bilbao.  The stadium is called San Mames and it is beautiful! It's brand new, build in 2007, and holds 53,000. 


They played Augsberg for the Europa cup (its a tournament for the teams that didn't qualify for the Champions League (Champions League is a a very prestigious international soccer playoff tournament).  They ended up winning 3-1!! The atmosphere there was great! There are so many songs and cheer and chants. Someone will start one, but then the entire stadium will join in.  Its pretty spectacular.


A very curious thing happened on during half time.  Everyone whipped out a tin foil wrapped sandwich.  When I say everyone, I mean like 90% of the people.  It was really bizarre and kind of creepy, but I guess everyone here likes to have a sandwich in between halves.

Me and my friend Alex after the game

This weekend we decided to go over to San Sebastian for the weekend. Its only about an hour away by bus and the tickets are about $15 round trip! Our bus was at 7:30 AM and we (but really it was just me because I thought I had time for another bowl of cereal) almost missed the bus, BUT we made it and everything worked out!

perks of early buses: seeing the sunrise over the mountains

We wandered around in the beautiful city for a little while and then we headed over to where we were going to stay.



We also decided to drop into a nearby cafe and grab a little something for breakfast.


So here is where we stayed.  We used Airbnb to book this room.  Airbnb is an app that you can use to book rooms in other peoples houses.  Think of it as Uber for rooms in your house.  It was a little sketchy, but you are able to talk to the person and see pictures and she was highly rated previous people.

view from the outside

We had a little trouble trying to figure out the extra bed situation.  They lady said that they had an extra bed in the room that we could use, but we were looking around in the closets and couldn't find anything.  I volunteered to go down and ask the lady where the extra bed was.  She didn't speak English and so when she was explaining to me that you just go up to one of them and "lift the bed up and the extra bed is underneath", I thought I wasn't understanding right.  I asked her to repeat it and she said the same thing.  I was pretty confused. I told her to come show me.  We then found out that one of the beds was sneakily disguised as a bunk bed.  In reality, all you had to do was lift the bed up!!

 It was actually a very scary bunk bed. It looked like it was 30 years old and the top bed was held up by one small metal tube.  So we just pulled the mattress out and put it in the middle of the floor



Here is the bathroom, because I know my mom will want to see.  

yup, there is no curtain...

We made our way back to the touristy Casco Viejo and had an amazing lunch. It was a little pricey, it was a touristy area, but it tasted sooo good!!

Ham, chicken, green pepper kabob with potato

5 cheese ravioli with walnuts on top

After our filling lunch, we walked over to the beach.  This beach is famous for surfing and I was hoping to find a place to take lessons.  The past couple weeks, I had been doing research on surf lessons, but most of them were week long camps or weekend camps.  I was more looking for a 1 or 2 hour lesson.  I told my group that surfing was something I wanted to try and do here and I was surprised that the whole group was also interested. 

As we were walking along the board walk the first thing I saw was a couple surf boards right next to a hole in the wall.  It didn't look convincing, but I decided to try. It ended up being a great option.  They got us all in a 1 hour private lesson later for about $28 (surfboard and wetsuit included!).  It was awesome! The instructor was nice, but he honestly didn't teach that much.  He showed us how to stand and then would give us a boost and push us into waves.  


Even though he wasn't a big help, I stood up and was able to ride a few waves! I was so happy to finally be able to cross this one off my bucket list! I really want to go back to a nearby beach and rent a board for a few hours.

After that awesome adventure we decided to hike up this mountain near the beach in order to see the sunset! We had to haul to get up in time, but the views were amazing.


There was a dark and skinny stairway to the top of the mountain!


There was a really cool old fortress on top that we had fun climbing around on.

titanic?

I promise that it was worth climbing on top of that ledge!! I got some beautiful pictures and a couple amazing photospheres!



San Sebastian Photosphere



See!!! Look how awesome this one is!!

Also, there is a huge statue of Jesus on top of the fortress.


After that long hike, we went to get some of the famous pintxos in the old town area of San Sebastian.  They were pretty good!


When we got home that night, we were all super exhausted and ready to crash.  Then at 12:00 AM my friends surprised me with a cake that they had bought behind my back! It was really nice and made the weekend really special.  


They forgot a knife and so we had to cut it with floss! ahahah


The next morning we awoke at 9:00 and had a little breakfast that was provided by the owner. I ate lots of nutella toast.


We then headed over to another mountain and walked along another beach that is in San Sebastian.


There are also some beautiful houses along the beach.


We were artsy and spelled out "Bilbo" with our shadows.  That means Bilbao in Basque.


Instead of hiking up the mountain, we took the venicular up the mountain.



A two minute ride is enough to take a nap right?

The views at the top were incredible.  I think this mountain was my favorite part of my trip.  The weather was beautiful and the sky was clear. I could have sat up there for hours.


There was also a carnival on top.  It was a little bizarre.   


its impossible to escape the wrath of Caterpillar

 Next we tackled this giant watch tower. Notice how it is higher than the trees and all other buildings?? That's what I was really excited about!


They had some cool historical stuff inside and also a really old elevator.

I highly suggest that no one ever ride this.
But I the real reason I wanted to go up was because of the breath taking views like this. 


Click the link for the photosphere to get the full view.

Monte Igueldo Photosphere

We really wanted to ride this 103 year old roller coaster, but the workers went on a 2 hour lunch (this is typical Spanish work ethic for you!!). To kill time, we talked with one of the shopkeepers.  It was a little intimidating, but it was so rewarding!! She was so nice! We chatted about school and why we were studying abroad, but then she told us all about the history of the park and the town.  We also learned some new Basque words and also got some great travel recommendations from her! It was one of my big highlights of the whole weekend!

When the workers finally came back, we were able to ride the roller coaster!!! The shop keeper let us keep our bags behind her counter and even took a video of us!

only a little sketch

Here is a video I took on the roller coaster. Notice that there are no seat belts and the only thing holding me in was that tiny little chain.



When we finally returned to Bilbao, we had dinner! I was realllllly craving "Cravings" but since that was kinda too far, I had to compromise with generic Chinese food.




When I got my home, my host mom surprised me with a gift! She got me a Athletic scarf and a bracelet!


Okay, so the week is almost over! I promise!! On Sunday morning was the final for rowing! We decided it would be cool to view the regatta from the top of the Puente Colgante.  So we did!


 For a little bit at least, and then we went down to be a part of the crowd of supporters along the river.



A Basque team called Kaiko ended up winning, and the crowd was very pleased!


SOOOOO!!! If you made it this far, I am going to introduce a new section. This is where I will just put fun facts/ interesting things/ things I've learned.  I've seen some other people doing it on their blogs and I wanted to try it. So here we go!!


1.)  Almost everyone goes home and eats lunch with their family at about 1:00 or 2:00. They eat and talk and bond and such for a couple hours and then go back to work.  Its a very common thing, and if you try and go to a store at that time, its almost guaranteed to be closed

2.)  They have weird sized batteries here.  I don't know why, and I don't know what they are used for, I just found them at the store.


3.) They are super big about their trash and recycling here.  In this picture here you can see that there are four separate spots. There is one for organic, glass, plastic, and paper.  I was talking to one of my teachers and he said that in his house, they even collect oil to be recycled.


4.) They don't have their own garbage bins here and everyone walks their garbage to one of these and then they are emptied regularly.  The cool part is that to open it, you don't need to touch the lid! You just step on that metal bar at the bottom and the top will open!


5.) Change here is a big deal.  There are 1 and 2 Euro coins that are exchanged regularly.  It is difficult to get used to carrying change and its still annoying, but I'm starting to get used to grabbing coins out of my pocket instead of my wallet to pay for that pastry.

There are so many more things that I have learned, but I will share those later! This weekend I'll be headed to Madrid with my school program, so that should be exciting! Hasta luego!!

title: One Month Down
content:
If you didn't hear, my passport finally came in! I'm glad this long journey is finally over! The only thing that I still have to do is get another visa, because the visa was printed inside the passport which I lost.  My study abroad office is taking care of that now, but I will not have a visa for this next weekend when I go to London.  They have told me that I have sufficient paper work to prove that I am in Spain legally, but we will find out for sure next Monday when I come back!



My host mom makes some amazing fried chicken! We had some sweet peppers with it and it was amazing!! 


One day after class we went to a bar to get tapas after class and I tried squid with squid ink or maybe it was octopus with octopus ink. Either way, the ink is tasteless! It just makes your mouth and teeth black for a few minutes.


When I go to my internship, I don't have time to eat lunch at home. So Begoña packs me a lunch to heat up in the microwave a work.  Usually I get some main course, and always a fruit, a piece of bread, and a juice box. Its so nice of her to do it and the food is always great!  

The main course here is a soft boiled egg over rice with a really yummy tomato sauce

One day I realized that I had a meeting at 2:00 that day and so I wouldn't be able to go home and eat. But I realized that in the morning and I forgot to tell Begoña.  So I just did lunch on my own.  Originally, I was just going to grab a snack from the cafe in my school.  Then I realized that I had converted the 24 hour time to 12 hour time wrong and that my meeting was at 4:00 instead of 2:00....That was stupid, but definitely better than thinking it was at 4:00 when it was actually at 2:00!

Because I had extra time I decided to try this pizza place that I had been walking past for the past month.  I order the classic, but it didn't really seem classic.  First off, fries? Why fries with a pizza? I guess it works, but its still a little bizarre.  The pizza had decent toppings.  The onions were fresh, and the mushrooms weren't bad. The bacon was kinda plasticy, I'm not really sure if it was real bacon or not.  The worst part though was the sauce.  The sauce was the absolute worst part, because there was NO SAUCE! How do you make a pizza without sauce??? That's called cheese and bread not a pizza! I was frustrated, but at least the Coke tasted great.


After eating all that yummy (and not so yummy) food this week, I decided I should start to get back into running shape.  I started my first day of running by taking a route up the side of the port and out onto the coast.  It was a beautiful run at sunset.  




On Thursday I had my first meeting with my Tandem Conversation partner.  This program is organized by the university and the idea is that you pair native speakers with people who are trying to learn theat language.  So you pair a native Spanish speaker who wants to learn English with a native English speaker who wants to learn Spanish.  They do it for other languages too! 

The meeting was great! We had messaged before on Facebook and WhatsApp, but this was the first time we talked face to face.  He's a freshman at the University of Deusto, he plays soccer for a local club team and is a real fun guy to hang out with. 



On Friday, some of us decided to check out some food trucks that were out along the river one day.  The trucks were old Citroen and they were super interesting.  I had my first Mexican food since I arrived. It was an awesome burrito!



After the food trucks we went to see a flamenco show.  I think that most of us thought it was going to be just dancing, but it ended up being almost exactly the opposite.  It was mostly a concert given by a group of 5 people although there was one male dancer that came out for a few songs. He was really good and the show was definitely worth the $13


Beach Day!


On Saturday, we made our way to Sopelana beach.  It is only two metro stops away from my apartment so its super close.  I actually ran there! The path that I run on is above those cliffs that are by the beaches. 


We walked out onto this very scary skinny ledge to take some awesome pictures.  



It was actually kinda terrifying to take photos up there.  I tried to take a photosphere, but because the colors of the ground and the sand were so similar, It stitched the picture kind of weird and I didn't really want to venture out to take another one.

Not So Great Photosphere of Sopelana Cliff



We went surfing again for a couple hours.  It was really fun, but the waves weren't as big as when we went the other day.  I think it was just the time of day we went because size of the waves depends on the tides.

The instructor had us do some weird stretches




The scary thing about surfing here was that there was a ton of rucks under the water and they weren't that deep below.  They were probably only 5 feet below.  The instructor even taught us a special way to fall in order to protect ourselves.




Sunday Hike!!


On Sunday I got to go on my first hike!  It is with a club through the university and they meet every 2 weeks to go hiking somewhere.  I anticipated that it would be mostly students, but in reality it was mostly study abroad students and some some adults. 

We took an hour bus ride our to Markina.  We stopped by the 1000 year old Temple of San Miguel.  Apparently it used to be a place of pagan worship, but then when Christianity spread, they built a church around it.  Over the years it has been refurbished, but it has always been in the same spot. 

Thanks for standing in front of it Kelly

Now we started our journey up the mountain.  This was not your average hike.  It was more like a climb. The total elevation of the mountain was 2300 ft and we were moving at a pretty good pace.  Immediately when we started hiking, it started raining, so that was a little bit of a bummer.  

Instead of trying to tell you all about it, I made a short little video compilation of the journey.



I was realllllllly tired after the hike but it was totally worth it for the views! I have some pictures below for people who can't watch the video.


Hey Look!! A friend!!

Gotta stop for a quick snack!


Even more friends!!




Interesting Things About Spain



As I promised last week, I am going to tell you guys about some of the interesting things I've seen here.

Door Have Handles in the Middle of the door


This one actually kinda mad me mad.  Why would you do that? You don't get good leverage, it makes it incredibly awkward to open and close doors, and it looks weird.  I don't get it at all.




Escalators Change Speed when no one is on them.  


I'm not 100% sure how this works, but I know it has to do with a pressure pad at the top and bottom of the escalator.  If someone doesn't step on the platform for a while, it slows down to about a quarter of the speed, but as soon as someone walks across the bottom, it speeds up again.  It seems like a pretty ingenious and simple idea to save some energy.



Everyone Smokes


A ton of people here smoke and they do it a lot.  It always surprises me when I walk out side of school and there is hundreds of kids outside smoking.  Every where you walk on the street, there is someone within 8 feet of you with a lit cigarette. 


Commercial breaks are long a few


Commercials are not done in short burst like in the US.  They are done in gigantic chunks.  Some of the commercial breaks are 7 minutes long!



No one texts here


Everyone uses WhatsApp.  Its basically an instant messaging service that is registered under your phone number.  So its texting, but instead messages are sent through WiFi or data.  Its kind of incredible how much it is used.  For example, instead of texting your vote on a game show you send it through WhatsApp.  Or if there is an advertisement that wants you to send a message to get more info or join a promotion, it asks for a WhatsApp message not a text message.


So that wraps up this blog post!  Next week's post might be a little late because I will be traveling to London this weekend until Monday and I don't think I will bring my laptop. See ya!!

title: Week 8
content:
This week was pretty relaxing.  The weather was great and we had no big trips planned for the weekend, even though we ended up doing plenty of things!


I decided to get another Tandem partner last week.  I was a little unsure about the decision because I wasn't sure if I would have enough time.  I had a couple meetings with him so far and they have been really great! I'm glad I decided to have a second one! 

Another think I went to this week was an eramsus exchange.  Erasmus is the European Union Study Abroad program and so student groups hold erasmus events for all foreign students.  It was fun talking to a fresh set of faces.  A lot of the people were actually not in school, in fact most that I talked to had already graduated, but it was fun nonetheless.

Remember how I told you that I my host mom is an excellent cook? Here is some more evidence of that from this week.

Fish with sweet peppers

Garbanzo beans with spinach

Pagassari


After my Europe in the World class I was chatting with the professor and a couple other students.  We were talking about our upcoming weekend and he suggested that we hike Pagasarri mountain.  He told us that it like the Bilbao mountain.  It is very very common for people to be hiking it everyday, even though the majority of the people will go Sunday morning.  
So naturally, we decided to head up there on Friday! The base of the mountain was a little hard to find, but luckily we had internet to quickly find some directions and get back on track.  Once we got to the base of the mountain, the signs were easy to follow.

The hike was excellent! It was a beautiful day and the path was gorgeous!



Oh and the views of the city and the ocean were amazing as well!



The hike took us about 2 hours and it was about 1800 ft high.  At the top there was a bar where we all got some well deserved pintxos and water and enjoyed the view





Here are some photospheres from the hike!


Pagasarri Photosphere 1

Pagasarri Photosphere 2

I keep going on all these hikes and I love it! The nearby area is very hilly and so there are many places to visit.  They all have such good views too! I'm going to be a master hiker at the end of this year.


Later that night, we got a small group together and went over to the cliffs by the ocean.  We played Heads Up (its like team catchphrase) in Spanish and it was so much fun! 


Santander


The next day we took a short little trip to Santander. Its a small beach town about 1.5 hr bus ride away.  We intentionally didn't plan much so that we could have a very relaxed day.

As you can see, we left Basque Country, because no one would ever fly a Spanish flag that big in Bilbao


While we were strolling through the town, we noticed that they had these little trees everywhere. They looked more like roots that trees!


Before heading to the beach we decided to have lunch first! For first course I had a very typical Spanish salad with tuna and a plethora of oil, vinegar and salt.


Second course was fried eggs, french fries and chorizo


For dessert I had strawberry cake


And then of course we got second dessert!


So we finally made it to the beach and it was beautiful!


We wandered through the Piquio Gardens


And we even made some new snail friends



Piquia Garden Photosphere


We then headed off to see the royal palace, but on the way we got some more great views


We even passed through a zoo and so we saw the seals and sea lions!


We finally arrived at the Royal Palace/ Castle building! Again the views around here were amazing as well!




The Grand Lunch


Begoña has been telling me about this big lunch that she always makes for her study abroad students for quite some time.  Finally, this Sunday was the day.  It was quite the ordeal though!  At 3:00, we started by going down to a bar to have pintxos.  Keep in mind that they have lunch very late here. There we met up with her nephew, her nephews wife and one of Begoña´s friends. We returned home at about 4:30 and started eating at 5:00.  It was more like a big dinner. 



First course was another typical basque salad


But the main course was squid and squid ink.  Begoña kept teasing and telling me that it was actually crude oil.  It really wasn't bad at all, it was actually pretty good.  The ink doesn't taste like anything.  Its just a little salty, but that could have just been from the squid.  Either way, the meal was very good!



This week was much more relaxed and it was a great break from all the busy traveling.  This upcoming weekend I have a trip to the South of France with my program, so that should be fun!

title: Playing Catch Up
content:
So. A lot has happened, but I have been busy and a little lazy and haven't been keeping up with this blog.  So this post is going to be quite lengthy. I'm going to try and cover about a week and a half of content, so be prepared! 

So where  I left off last update was with our tour off Bilbao!  This tour was great for me and really opened my eyes to the history and culture of Bilbao and the Basque Country.

In this picture below, you can see the river and the Guggenheim Museum that is soooooooo close to my school!! This museum is amazing and I love it so much.  I went on a tour of it recently, and I am going to make a post dedicated to just the museum because its that awesome.


another picture of the Guggenheim I took that day.
So I took that first picture on top of this bridge that goes across the river and connects the two sides of Bilbao.  Its right in front of the university and connects it to the downtown area.  I went back later and took a photosphere on top of that bridge. For those of you who don't know, a photo sphere is kind of like a panoramic picture except instead of it being in a circle, its a sphere!! Its kind of like Google Earth when you can go on the street level and look around and stuff. You can click and drag to move around and up and down and explore. Here is the link to the one that I took on the bridge.

Bridge Photosphere

The things that will stick out are the school (which is what you are pointed at initially), and the Guggenheim. But also notice the Deusto sign on the silver building that is right off the end of the bridge on the opposite side of the river as the rest of the University. That is the new library.  Next to this you will see the Iberdrola tower. This is the utility company of most of Spain. Originally, to me the tower was obtrusive and annoying because it disrupted the old historic feel of Bilbao, but its starting to grow on me. I like that its curved and full of glass. It doesn't feel as industrial as some skyscrapers in Chicago and so that helps it blend more with the city.

This is the spot where soccer was first played in Bilbao. This plaque is right along the river and very close to the Guggenheim museum. The plaque is a poem that talks about how the workers would play during breaks and after shifts.  It says that sometimes the ball would go into the river and they would throw rocks to make ripples to push the ball back towards them.


Next we made our way over to Casco Viejo, which is like the old town.  Its pretty touristy, filled with restaurants and bars and stores.  I actually saw a story on the news that the Bilbao government was going to ban any more bars and restaurants from opening because there were already too many. Anyways, even though its touristy, you still find awesome things like this cathedral


Its actually falling over, and so they build some new supports on the side, but even that is falling over as well! You can see in the picture below how that stone column gets moves farther and farther left as you move to the top.


Random street photo where you can see all the beautiful architecture.


We saw this outdoor theater close by the river as well.  It has a really cool floating roof and the stained glass on the back wall are beautiful. There is also a little bar underneath the whole thing as well! Oh yah, its called Arenal Kiosk or Kiosko Arenal.




One day the Soccer team here had an open house where you could walk around the stadium and take a picture with the cup. The line was really long so we only took pictures of the stadium.  Its pretty awesome and I can't wait to go to a game!


Here's a random Photophere I took in front of the business building at my school.  Notice again the giant tower.

University of Deusto: Stairs in front of Business Building

There are tons of plaza's every where like this one. It makes the city much prettier by adding more green space.  This happens frequently with the traffic circles.  They fill the inside with a fountain and flowers and a nice walking path.  Its great and I wish we did that in the US.


Here is another photo sphere I took in one of the other Plazas called Plaza Moyua.  Sorry the fountain got messed up. I'm not sure how that happened. I'm still perfecting this whole Photosphere thing.

Plaza Moyua


Later that weekend my host mom brought me to the cliff/beach area that is right at the mouth of the river that eventually flows through Bilbao.




One day there was an British cruise ship in the port so we went to the beach to watch it leave.  There was also a bunch of old people walking around Bilbao speaking English, so that was a little refreshing.


On Wednesday, a group of about 4 of us decided to see The Sister Act at this beautiful 
theater called Teatro Arriaga.  It was in Spanish, but since it was a musical, the actors spoke very clearly and articulated very well.  The show was easy to follow and I understood a lot of it! It was well worth the 22 Euro.
Picture from the outside. You can't see this, but it is right on the river!



Inside atrium area

The view from the highest of the highest seats! but hey it was like $25

One day we decided to go up the mountain side to see the city from up there.  It was an amazing view.  Sadly it was cloudy, but that's how it is here most of the time unfortunately.   I really want to go back up and see the city at night. I've seen beautiful pictures from other people who went up at night.



On Friday, I was writing postcards at my desk, and I put two arms on the desk, and then the back two wheels broke off! I freaked out quite a bit and I was angry that I broke it.  I looked down at the wheels and noticed that the piece of wood it was mounted to, was too small. Thus each wheel only could fit two screws when each one needed four. 

The next day, I let Begoña know that I had broken it. I was a little afraid to tell her and kinda embaressed I did it.  When I told her, she told me that she knew it was unstable and that she knew it was going to break.  She said it wasn't a big deal and that she had a board she wanted to use to fix it.  I said "Okay! Let's do it tomorrow!". She laughed and asked me if I was serious. Of course I was serious! So most of Sunday went towards fixing this desk. 

It was definitely an interesting experience.  I learned a ton of new words and taught Begoña some new tricks.  As you can see, we ended up doing all of the woodwork in her small kitchen.  It was kinda cramped which made it pretty unique.  I've never cut a board that was halfway out of a kitchen window, and then had a 60 year old woman sitting on the counter to keep it from moving.  It was a new experience for sure.
this picture really doesn't do it justice

One of my favorite things that happened this week was when we went to Puente Colgante.  Its definitely top 3 favorite things of this city.  I love how big and outrageous it is.  It is such an interesting take on the problem of boat and car traffic.  The bridge has been around forever, 1893 actually.  The technical name is transporter bridge and there are only 12 still running in the world.  It was partially destroyed by Franko during the Spanish Civil War, but they fixed it up and its as good as new!



I didnt take this next picture, but I wanted to give you guys a better look at how the ferry thing attaches to the bridge part.



We went both across on the ferry ship thing and we also walked across the top of it. So here is two pictures from our trip across on the ferry.


And then here are some pictures from the top.  Its so beautiful from up top.  You can see so far! Its also realllllllylyyyyy high. and it shakes when the ferry goes across and sways a little in the wind.  I didn't like that at all.  However, it was worth it for the views!


I found it interesting that it looks like a truss bridge, but its actually a suspension bridge, they just hide it really well.  

Yes, I'm a nerd.


I put my phone through the wire mesh and I risked its life for this panorama, so you better look at it 



Also, a photosphere too, because I think they are so cool!!

Puente Colgante


Oh yah, and one random day we went to Plentzia beach, Its super pretty and it was a lot of fun! We swam out to the boueys and talked to some open water swimming. We body surfed.  We kind of saw the sunset.  It was behind the mountain and it was kinda cloudy so it didn't really look that nice.


I really want to come back here and hike the mountain and rent kayaks and go down the river or maybe out on the ocean.



Also....another Photo Sphere. You guys gotta tell me if you like them, because I think they're awesome, but if you don't look at them then I'll stop putting them in here.

Plentzia Beach

Okay, people.  Thats basically all I have for now.  I'm going to try and get better at posting regularly on Sunday and covering the previous week. Stay tuned!!

title: France, Painted Forest, and Butrón Castle
content:
As October comes to an end, I am still amazed that I walk around in a t-shirt,  The weather has barely changed.  Its actually kind of funny because my host mom always tells me its chilly and that I should take my jacket.  When really its like 60 degrees outside. I guess that's how I would feel if I was spoiled with such nice weather.  Even though its not that great, there is quite a bit of rain.  Because of that, I always have an umbrella in my backpack. 

It took me a while, but I finally succumbed.  I had McDonalds for the first time.  I'm really good about going out a trying new foods, but this Wednesday I couldn't fight that smell of fries.


Oh and the food wasn't different in anyway. Which means the fries were AMAZING! Nothing beats McDonalds fries, except Gene and Judes. The only weird thing was that the menu was only half translated, so I had to say McNugget with a Spanish accent so they could understand.  


I've noticed lately that my weeks have become a little boring.  I tend to go to school and go immediately home.  I don't really take advantage of my weekdays as much as I used to.  This is mostly because I have more school work and applications. Nevertheless, the weeks are slow.  I was talking to Celina about this and she challenged me to see something new everyday.  Even if it was as simple as walking home a different way.  I thought this was a great idea, and so it is something I strive to do everyday.  It has been really helpful so far and I have actually found a lot!

For example, one day I decided to do homework outside.  So I found this quaint plaza by the river with a beautiful fountain.  


Bilbao Fountain Photosphere

The best part though was that when I was walking to the metro, this poster caught my eye.


You can rent pogo stick boots! They look super fun! I've seen them online, so we will have to see if I have time to try them out!

This was a little lucky, but I was walking home one day and I noticed that the streets were closed. All the cars were honking and people were yelling at the police that blocked the street.  I decided to stay.  I was afraid to ask the officer because I didn't want to look like an idiot because I didn't know what was going on and because I didn't want to speak Spanish to him.  So instead I eavesdropped and eventually I found out that the King was coming through.  Apparently he likes to come here to spend time along the coast.  After about half an hour (yes the cars were pissed!!) the King came flying through the traffic circle.  There was quite a large convoy; a few police on motorcycles, a couple police cars, about three Mercedes, and an ambulance.  However, through the backseat window, I was able to see the King! 


Another day I saw one of the most ridiculous vehicles I have ever seen.  This thing would look weird in the US, but in Europe it looks like a monster truck.  I have no idea what this is for, but it looks like a military Humvee had a baby with a truck camper. 



South of France

So Friday morning we left on a tour bus to go to the south of France.  This trip was pretty fun! It was only one day long and I really wish it was longer.

Before we get started, I made this short video with some videos that I took this weekend.  You can either watch it now, or read a little bit and come back to watch it once you know what everything actually is!



We started in San Juan de Luz.  This town is know for its royal wedding and hosted many during the 17th and 18th century.  Now it is a popular beach side resort.



And I can definitely see why people come here for the beach!


We briefly walked into a church for a few minutes and I absolutely loved the woodwork!



After we had our short little tour of the city, we had some free time.  We spent all of it eating in the market and at different pastry shops.  


We had macaroons


and baguettes 


and of course croissants!


The food was great here. Well it was mostly pastries, not really food, but great nonetheless.


Lunch was absolutely incredible.  The appetizers were these peppers stuffed with some kind of fish in a sweet sauce.


The next part was one of my favorites.  It was just a giant salad with heaping amounts of meat.  There was bacon, salami, chorizo, and Iberian ham.  It was ridiculously good. I had quite a lot of that dish.


Next came our main course.  Duck with French fries.  I had never tried duck before, and it was very good.  The meat was really savory and had a lot of flavor.  


Dessert was this pastry that kinda reminded me of a pie.  The crust was similar at least and then there was a thin sugary spread on top.


After the amazingly delicious lunch, we hopped on the bus and left for Biarritz. This is a small town on the coast of France and it is a very popular tourist location.  We had very little time here though.  In reality, we only had about 2 hours.  However, I’m very glad we stopped because this was some of the most beautiful coast line I have ever seen.  There was an unnatural amount of mist or fog in the air and around the coast.  Our teachers didn’t know what it was and so I don’t think it happens very much.  However, it did make for some fairy tale esque photos.  When we arrived, we immediately headed for the coast to go on a little walking tour.


The ocean was very rough today and the waves were splashing up onto the pier!



I really wanted to walk out on the pier, but my professor said we couldn't. I'm not a 100% sure why, maybe he thought it was too dangerous because of the waves, but I don't really know.

Biarritz Ocean Photosphere

We had some gelato which means that Lauren turns into Pinocchio


Most of the time, it felt like a was on a different planet  


So once we finished walking down the coast with our group, we were allowed about 30 minutes of free time.  I reallyyyyy wanted to go back and venture out on the pier. I would have to go back the way we came and move farther away from where we were getting picked up, so I ran.  

I think this was one of the best decisions I have made this trip because the pictures I took of that pier at dawn were unbelievable.








Oma and the Painted Forest


On Saturday we rounded up a pretty big group to go out to see the Painted Forest.  We jumped on a bus and rode it out into the country side for about an hour. When we got off, it took us a while to figure out where we needed to go, but after asking about 4 different people, we were on the right path.


Along the way we found a fig tree and these fruits are quickly becoming one of my favorites.





 Finally we arrived at the painted forest.  This was created by a painter and sculptor name Agustin Ibarrola.  




Many of the paintings need to be viewed from certain angles and these spots are marked by small triangles. 


Sometimes many trees were involved to make one simple shape.  These were my favorite because of how continuous the circle looks, but some trees are much closer to me than the others.



Painted Forest Photosphere 1

Painted Forest Photosphere 2

 Just walking around in the country side was great. I love how green everything is here.  I guess all the rain that we get does have some benefits.


Out in the distance, we noticed a castle.  Because its just normal to have random castles everywhere in Spain.


When we got there, it sounded like there was some kind of party going on inside, but we weren't really sure. 


Oh and we met a really cute dog along the way!




Butrón and Armintza

On Sunday I wasn’t really planning on doing anything, but at about 10:00 my host mom came in my room and told me we were going to a castle!  She had told me before that she was going to take me eventually, but this was unexpected.


The castle is actually very close to my house (about 15 min by car) but it is difficult to get to by bus, which is why she needed to drive me there. The castle is very pretty and dates back to the Middle Ages

The castle used to open up to the public and you could go inside and explore. You can even hold events there like the one by the painted forest.  However, this didn´t work out and it has been closed for about 15 years.  After taking some pictures at the castle, we left to go visit Armintza.




Arminza is a very small fishing town a few miles up the coast from Bilbao.


The views from the town were great!



The whole time we were taking pictures, I was thinking about how cool it would be to climb up on that tall rock. But I was afraid Begoña wouldn't approve and she would yell at me.  But I was wrong. She told me to go up before I even asked!



It was totally worth it.  I got this awesome panorama!



After we hung around here for a little, we decided it was time for lunch. Begoña decided to take me to a restaurant that was close by.  She insisted that I try halibut. I had never had halibut before, but it was really good! I think it was my favorite fish that I've had so far!


Oh yah and I took this picture a little ways down from the restaurant.  I know its hard to see, but the wind was pretty strong and it was blowing the white caps back and making a rooster tail like thing over the waves. It might be easier if you go back and watch the video.  It was a really cool thing and I've never seen anything like it.



Something else this weekend was that Begoña finally got to speak with my family.  She speaks very little English, and so she was able to greet them and that was about it.  In reality, that was the most English that I have ever heard her speak.  No one is fluent in Spanish in my family and even those who did know Spanish found it hard to understand her.  It made sense though because Skyping with a weak internet connection is bad enough when you know the language.  So because of this, I got to translate.  It was actually really fun! I always like translating, but I usually don't have many opportunities to translate for people.

So that wraps up this weeks blog! Next week I will be heading to Sevilla for the weekend!

title: Solo in Sevilla
content:
Not a whole lot happened this week, so I am mostly going to talk about my trip to Sevilla.

On Tuesday I filled up my pay as you go SIM card with 10 Euro and I won half of a GB of data! This was pretty awesome for me because so many of my friends use Facebook and WhatsApps to communicate.  I wasn't able to use the data though, it wasn't working.  So the next day I went to the Orange store (my phone carrier) and I tried to figure out what was wrong.

In the past, I would read tech articles in Spanish and I'm so glad I did that because talking with those sales people would have been impossible! I eventually figured out that I needed to activate a different plan and change some settings.  However, as I found out this weekend, that didn't actually work.  So I need to go back and fix that. 


Zuricalday


Also on Tuesday I went to Zuricalday, which is a pretty well known pastry shop. The reason you go on Tuesday though is because everything is half price!

This one was like a soft cake bread with pudding on top.


This one is a flaky bread covered in chocolate!


Something weird also happened that Tuesday, I was the only person on the metro for about 3 stops which was eerie.



Record Store


So one of my friends Lauren needed to buy a gift for her host dad's birthday and she was thinking about getting him a vinyl record of classic American rock band because apparently he really likes that stuff.  So of course I volunteered to go with and the store was awesome! It was like any record store, but there was a ton of Spanish music.  I didn't have much time to browse because we went on Thursday and I had to leave to catch my flight. But that's okay, it gives me more reason to go back!


Sevilla


First off, I have made friends here. I didn't travel alone because I'm smelly, I did it because I thought it was something I should do. Many people have told me that traveling alone is an experience that everyone should have. No, I didn't "find myself" or have some big revelation on life, but it still was an awesome experience.

I got to the airport with plenty of time and the flight went flawlessly, we actually were 15 minutes ahead of schedule! Unbelievable, I know.


After a bus ride and asking for directions a couple times (the streets are very difficult to navigate!) I finally made it to my hostel. The hostel was clean and actually kinda pretty. The staff was also very helpful!


As soon as I arrived, I dropped off my stuff, grabbed a very essential map and headed out.


One of the big things on my list was going to see "Las Setas" which means "The Mushrooms".  This is actually a relatively new structure that was built completely out of wood in 2011.  People say its ugly, but I think its pretty cool! 


As you can see its really difficult to photograph this thing because it was so big, so I highly encourage you to look at the photosphere I took from underneath because I think it does a much better job at capturing this thing.

Underneath Las Setas Photosphere

You also can pay 3 Euro and go up on top of Las Setas! I went up during sunset which was a great idea!


I also took some photospheres up top.

On top of Las Setas Photosphere 1

On top of Las Setas Photosphere 2


While I was at Las Setas, I met a couple of American girls who were studying in Sevilla. I walked around the city with them for a little bit and then they helped me find where my flamenco show was.


I reserved a spot in a Flamenco show at a place called La Casa de La Guitarra and I the best seat in the house. I was front row right in the middle and the chair even had my name on it!


I think that I could actually reach out and touch the performers.


This show was about an hour long and they showcased some different styles of flamenco from different areas of Spain. 

After the show I headed back to my hostel and hung out in the commons area.  I met a guy from Vancouver named Greg and two other Kiwi (that's what people from New Zealand call themselves) girls that he was traveling with.  They had been traveling for about 2 months and it was great to hear all their stories!

 The next day, I got up early so that I could grab some breakfast before I went to the free walking tour at 11:30.


But I actually had some extra time so I went to a little market and did some exploring. I ended up coming out with a kiwi watermelon juice and a pastry.



Me and Greg decided on doing the Spanish tour instead of the English one and it was by far the better option.  Instead of a group of 20 it was just us two and one other girl.  It was almost like a private tour! The girl was super nice and a great guide.  Her Spanish had a very southern accent, but she spoke very clearly and it was easy to understand.



During our tour, we got a nice overview of the city and some of the history behind it.  We learned about how it was founded by the Greeks, but captured by the Romans and then later the Moors. 


We walked through a lot of the city and saw many of the big tourist attractions from the outside, but we didn't actually go inside.  Don't worry though! I do have pictures, I'll just get to those later.

Plaza de Triumfa Photosphere

So we ended our tour in La Plaza de España.  This was such a beautiful place, there was a pond that ran around the center, and also a giant fountain in the middle. 


Running around the edges, there is a bench for each providence of Spain.


And you bet I went out and found Basque Country!


Also!! Nerdy Fun Fact of the Day: Star Wars Episode 1 and 2 were filmed here!!!



After the walking tour me and Greg got some lunch at a burger place, but hey! this was my first burger that I have had in Spain!


After our North American lunch, we headed back into the city to try and visit some of the places we saw.

Look at this tiny street!


The guy from our hostel told us that we could go into a smaller cathedral and then use that ticket to skip the lines in the bigger cathedral and the Giralda tower. So that's exactly what we did! The smaller cathedral was much smaller, but still very beautiful.


However, the bigger cathedral (Sevilla Cathedral) was amazing! This cathedral was the largest when it was built, although now it is only the third largest.  Construction started in 1184 as a mosque, but took over 400 years to complete.  Throughout that time, many different people influenced the design of the cathedral and it is easy to see the Moorish influence contrasting against the Roman influence.  


If you look at this picture you can see the difference between the dome structure and the rest of the Cathedral.


Everything inside was beautifully crafted and detailed.  Look at this ceiling!



We also saw one of the four tombs of Christopher Columbus.  Its kind of a mess with who actually has parts of his body and whats buried where so he actually might not even be buried here.


Next we went up the Giralda Tower. This is a big bell tower that is connected to the church, so I actually took this picture after I went up but I just wanted you to get a better idea. 


Even in the Tower you can see the difference in the Moorish architecture on the bottom, versus the Christian style on the top.


The views from the top were excellent! oh and that ugly tower out in the distance is locally know as the tube of lipstick.


Here is a photosphere I took in the plaza right next to the tower and the cathedral 

Cathedral and La Giralda Photosphere

After the Cathedral and the Giralda, me and Greg just started walking around the city.  We found so much green space! The gardens there were incredible. Everything was luscious and well kept.



They also have these orange trees everywhere. Except you can eat them because they are super sour.  Instead they import them to Britain and they make a jam.  In Britain its called "Jam from Sevilla" and in Sevilla its called "Jam from Britain".


We walked up along the river and made our way to the hostel.



We hung out in the hostel for the night.  We exchanged stories about our trips and our lives back and home. They hostel hosted a free dinner every night.  There is about 30 people that all get together and hang out in the common area and eat and talk and stuff. Its actually really cool and fun! I heard so many good stories and met a lot of people from around the world.

The next morning I got up pretty early to use all the daylight I could.  I said goodbye to Greg because he was on his last leg of his trip and he was going to catch a train to Madrid for his flight back home to Vancouver.  

Anyways, my first stop was the Alcazar.  This is a big royal palace that is still used to this day! Its very similar to Alhombra, because they both had very Moorish influences.  


I made the mistake of buying the Spanish audio tour instead of English.  I kinda forgot that the vocabulary describing the Moorish architecture of the Italian Renaissance era were a little out of my league.  Nevertheless, the palace was stunning! 


and the attention to detail was really incredible.


Oh yah, one thing about Sevilla is that they have some incredible tiles. They put tiles on everything in that city! Its really beautiful, and the Alcazar was amazing as well.


Like I said, one of my favorite parts of Sevilla was the gardens and the green space and the royal gardens were no exception! There was so much diversity in the plants and there was little fountains everywhere with tile benches to sit on and ponder life.



Again, like I said, the attention to detail was incredible. 




While I was inside the Alcazar I took a couple photospheres that you can check out!

The Alcazar (Small Plaza) Photoshere

The Alcazar (Main Plaza) Photosphere

The Alcazar (Garden) Photosphere

I was pretty hungry after that (mostly because I didn't have breakfast). So I went across the river and bought some salami, bread and a pastry from a couple different little stores. Then I had lunch on the side of the river! 



I also took a photosphere here if you are interested.

Puente de Isabel II Photosphere

After lunch I walked along the river north towards "La camara oscura" (the gloomy camera) and look at all the green space along the way!!


It was about a 30 minute walk to the tower. I paid 3 Euro and took an elevator up 100 ft to the top.  


So this tower is kinda like a periscope.  There is a screen like table that the image is projected onto.


and a hole in the ceiling allows the light to come in and project super clear pictures of the city.  The guy who operated the periscope, spoke Spanish and gave a good tour of the city.  The images were crystal clear and you could see people perfectly clear from about a mile away! It was really cool!


After the little tour, you could walk out on the balcony and see the great views first hand!



After the tower, I headed over to the bull fighting ring, but I got side tracked by this store called Taste of America.


I was very tempted to buy a lot of the things in that store, mainly the beef jerky, peanut butter, and Dr Pepper, but I ended up only walking away with my most favorite snack ever!! I apologize for the blurry picture, but I was very excited!


So I finally arrived in the stadium!  There was a short 45 minute tour that was given in Spanish and English. This was perfect, because I could practice my Spanish, but at the same time I still was able to understand everything about the stadium.


So a little history about bull fighting is that originally, the spectacle was about the men on horseback because they were the knights.  The show was not only for public entertainment, but also for practice for the knights.  As the shows became more popular,  the emphasis began to shift to the people who were on the ground on foot who were there to protect the knight if they were endanger.  Thus bull fighting as we know it was born


Fun fact, not all bulls are killed after the fight.  If the bull fighter believe that the bull put up a good battle, then he can appeal to the judges to have the bull live. If they agree, the bull is honored and eventually returned to the farmer.  The last time this happened in Sevilla was in 2008, but the bull died of natural causes in 2013. That bull is shown on the wall in the photo below.


After the stadium, I went to go see more of the gardens before sunset.


María Luisa Park Photosphere


I also returned to Plaza de España for a second time.


and I also took a photosphere

Plaza de España Photosphere


Walking back to the hostel there was a ton of people out in the "street". I say it like that because I don't really know what it was.  People would walk all over, but there was also a bike lane, a trolley would pass through occasionally, and there was always a horse and buggy driving around.


When I got back to the hostel it was time for the free dinner! It was garbanzo beans with chorizo.


and for dessert was oranges that we dipped in chocolate


I woke up pretty early to catch my flight so that I would have some time to walk around a little bit before heading of for Bilbao. I made it to the airport with plenty of time and I actually was able to start this blog post.

Landing in Bilbao was cool because we circled the city in a different way. So I got an amazing view of Bilbao!


So my final thought on traveling alone are that I don't think its bad at all. Like I said, I didn't find myself or come up with some crazy revelation.  I think that my views on it match up with most other people's.  I like that I can go my own speed and do whatever I want.  I love that I met some cool people and I generally felt more inclined to talk to people. However, it does get lonely sometimes and it is nice to share the experiences with someone else.

FUN FACTS!!

Stall Cracks

I'm not sure why stall cracks are so common in the US, but in Europe they basically don't exist.  I have no idea why, but the door always overlaps with the frame.

title: First Day On The Job
content:
So today was my first day at my internship. Well actually its technically a class and I get credit for it.  It was really rainy today so that was lame, but I found the company just fine and arrived still arrived 20 minutes early.  I had previously had a meeting with one of the employees of the company last week.  My "professor" for this class was there as well. I say professor like that because he's not really teaching, he coordinates the applications and the companies and I send him weekly summaries as well and my bigger mid-term and final report. Regardless, he is a super awesome guy and is super nice.

But anyways, the initial meeting was simply to break the ice and sign some papers.  I think it took all of about 15 minutes.  I definitely worried way more than I should have about it.

When I arrived to the company, RV CoolingTech, the same woman (her name is Susan) greeted me.  She is really nice and very accommodating. It was only us two there because all the other employees were either in a different country or on vacation. It’s a relatively small company, I think only about 10 employees.  The make ammonium based industrial HVAC (Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning) units (I learned a lot about what this was all about later in the day, but we will get to that in a sec). She didn’t really do much for me to do at all, really all I did productively was copy some papers for her. 

After that, she handed me a short booklet that had an overview of the company and the product that they make.  It was in English and in French, I don’t know why it wasn't in Spanish.  When I was reading it I found some errors.  They were small, and some of them weren't even errors, they were just better ways of saying things. 

It was interesting because when I saw the errors, it was pretty obvious that they were a native Spanish speaker and I could definitely see the thought process. Some of the grammar errors come from differences in structure between Spanish and English.   I found it funny because I struggle with those same differences, but just in the other direction!

 Susan is currently learning English as her 3rd language, so it helps that she can speak in English to explain some new words to me.  She has been very helpful so far with helping me learn as well.  She speaks very clearly and also very loudly (I think this is just her personality though) and so it is easy for me to understand.  When I learn a new word, she makes me repeat it, or if she corrects my sentence grammar, she will make me repeat it correctly.  I can already tell that this internship will be very beneficial for my Spanish. 

After I finished with that booklet, Susan told me that I could go on their website and learn more about their company  and what they do and what they stand for.  This got kind of repetitive and boring pretty quick, but I did learn a lot about HCAV and new laws and regulations. 

So the low down is that before about 10 years ago, everyone used chemicals that were terrible for the environment, but were really cheap and really efficient for HVAC.  Then stuff with global warming and ozone depletion happened and regulators are forcing companies to use less ozone harmful chemicals.  Ammonium is one of those chemicals.  Its not harmful to the environment, and its also very efficient.  The only thing is that its very toxic and also explosive.  There has been some incidents in the US in the recent years, but it appears that regulators are starting to crack down on safety and maintenance of these systems. So there is always pros and cons.

I don’t think that I will be copying papers all day for the rest of the semester either. I didn't totally understand what she was telling me, but I think I will be working underneath some one else for the rest of the semester.  He currently is in India for something, but will be coming back next week.  I should know more about what my future will look like then. 

I'm sorry there was no pictures in this post! Just lots of words.  To make up for that here is a picture of some awesome food that my host mom Begoña made for me.




That also reminds me that I am planning on making one giant post with all the food I have eaten so far. So prepare your belly for that one! Hasta Luego!

title: A Tour of the Apartment
content:
I will now show you my humble abode!  This is where I will be living for the next 4 months.  It is about a 5 minute walk from the metro and then school is about a 30 minute ride away.  Its kinda far, but so far it has been manageable.  My apartment complex is right next to a pretty popular square. There are a lot of restaurants, stores and bars around it. There are people on the square all day until everything closes at about 12 A.M. There are also quite a few events that happen there too.  There was an art festival where they set up a screen and projected art for a few hours. Another day, there was also an opera singer there for a couple hours. Its a pretty busy place! Also, one random thing; if the pictures are too small, you can click them and make them bigger (:

The plaza near my house
Anyways, lets get on with the tour!  So this is what you would see walking up to my door! My building is on the brick one on the left.  The construction is right out my window and can be kind of loud sometimes. 



I live on the "3rd floor" of my apartment building.  Fun Fact: In a lot of Europe, they don't start with 1 as the first floor, its 0. So I actually live on the second floor!



So this is what you see when you first walk in the door.  On the left is the salon/parlor room. and then at the end the hall way takes a right and leads to the rest of the house.


Notice the UIUC T-shirt in the mirror?

 Here is the parlor.  Notice on the left there are two guitars.  My host mom is a classical guitar teacher, so maybe I'll learn some this semester!


Now the is the rest of the hall way.  The first door on the left is the kitchen and another smaller room.  The second door on the left is my bathroom, and then the door at the end leads to the other bathroom and the two bedrooms.


First I will show you the kitchen.  Its quite compact, but it is definitely sufficient.  It looks like there is two dishwashers, but the one on the left is actually the clothes washer.  There is no dryer, they simply hang the clothes to dry.

There is a door in the kitchen that is a couple feet left of the dishwasher, which leads to this little lounge area. I'm not sure what to call it because I don't know what it would be called in the United States and she didn't tell me the name for it in Spain.  So I guess I'll call it the lounge.  The lounge is where I spend most of my time at home. This is also where I usually find Begoña. We will talk about our day, or about school, or share videos and pictures.  Some times we watch TV or a poorly dubbed movie.  Its a nice cozy space.  Again notice all the stringed instruments.
